bibliography.title: Solubility of He, Ne, Ar, Kr and Xe in a basalt melt in the range 1250–1600°C. Geochemical implications

scan.method: Visually read rendered pages. pdftotext returned page separators only. Adjacent articles on pp.400 and 409 are outside the review.

inspection_locations: p.402: Tables 1-2; Sections 2.1 and 2.2; Eq.1 C_i=S_i P_i.
p.403: Table 3, Section 2.2.6 and analytical methods.
pp.404-405: Tables 4-5, Eq.2, Figs.1-3 and uncertainty discussion.
pp.406-407: pressure/host limitations, vesicle model and Table 6.

host_and_conditions.host: MAPCO CH98-DR11 normal MORB tholeiitic basalt; Table 1 gives the starting glass composition and all Fe as FeO.
host_and_conditions.driving_quantity: Gas partial pressure, not a high-pressure fugacity law; C_i=S_i*P_i in Eq.1.
host_and_conditions.pressure_convention: Section 2.2.6 says total pressure one atmosphere; the abstract says 1 bar and Eq.4 discussion uses atmospheric P0=1 bar. Table 2 gas pressures are in 1e-6 bar. These printed conventions are retained without a silent 1.01325 rescaling.
host_and_conditions.interval_note: Marginal bounds for the seven nonblank He summaries, not a joint coverage rectangle. The 1250-1600 degC paper range includes other gases and is not the He Table 5 interval.

table_5_and_uncertainty.interpretation: p.404 describes a smoothed regression value at 1400 degC with one-sigma scatter about the regression. Table 5 prints 56.5 while the abstract/body print 56, all in 1e-5 units. This is not a standard error, a confidence interval for hot BSE, or a single measurement at 1400 degC.
table_5_and_uncertainty.temperature_fit: Eq.2 assumes Arrhenius behavior and suggests E about 30 kJ/mol for He; the authors call the temperature dependence weak and the heat of solution an order-of-magnitude estimate. No new Arrhenius extrapolation is fitted.
table_5_and_uncertainty.reconstruction_limit: Table 5 groups measurements by gas and temperature. Its seven He entries do not expose all 16 individual analyses or their row weights; no exact weighted-regression replay is claimed.

jambon1986.experimental_controls: Sections 2.2-3 check grain size, duration, gas mixing and quench/anneal loss. Air-equilibrated He results in Table 3 are not substituted for the preferred gas-mixture values in Table 5. Table 4 reports strong He loss on annealing at 600 degC; a full measurement error model is not reconstructed.

historical_ledger.result: The retained 0.00056 +/- 0.00011 at 1673.15 K matches the abstract/body. The full paper now adds the Table 5 precision 0.000565, actual He measurement interval, scatter meaning and controls. The ledger remains an immutable earlier abstract-only record.

guillot_sator.locations: PDF pp.12 (Section 3.1), 34 (Appendix B calibration) and 35 (Appendix C He/MORB row).
guillot_sator.scope: A scale comparison of reported coefficients in their printed STP/bar units at nominally 1400 degC; the 0.15 K labeling difference is retained. No unit rescaling, interpolation or significance test is applied.
guillot_sator.dependence: Guillot-Sator explicitly used Jambon (1986) and Lux (1987) MORB solubilities to tune the noble-gas/silicate interaction parameter to x=0.25. Agreement with Jambon is therefore not independent validation. Appendix B quotes Jambon He as 56.5 and rounds its own calculated He to 59; the provider uses the Appendix C value 59.6.

provider.result: The provider continues to interpolate the Guillot-Sator dry-host simulations and uses the explicit 273.15 K, 101325 Pa STP conversion. Jambon measurements are not adopted as runtime coefficients.
remaining_gaps: The Jambon MORB experiment does not calibrate olivine or wet BSE composition, 2173.15 K conditions or high-total-pressure corrections.
The provider gas-fugacity driving quantity and original low-pressure partial-pressure measurements need an application-specific comparison.
The source uses approximate atmospheric-pressure/STP language; no precise source-to-provider STP correction is inferred from the vesicle model reference T0=273 K and P0=1 bar.
Regression scatter, the approximate temperature slope and calibration-dependent MORB agreement do not establish a physical error bound.
